questions: Which structure sits outside the membrane in a plant cell?
Name the large storage space in the plant cell.
segments.say: A plant cell, labelled. Watch the labels land one by one: cell wall outside, membrane just inside, then nucleus, chloroplast and the big vacuole. Point at each structure on your student notes diagram as it appears.

questions: Which three plant structures are missing here?
What holds the animal cell together without a wall?
segments.say: An animal cell, labelled. Same membrane, nucleus and mitochondrion - but no wall, no chloroplast and no big vacuole. Tell your partner the three missing structures and what each one does.

questions: What crosses the membrane in this scene?
What gets refused, and why does that matter?
segments.say: The membrane is the gatekeeper. Watch closely: food crosses in, waste crosses out, and one particle is refused. The membrane chooses - it is selectively permeable, not a solid wall. Now try the membrane question on your worksheet.

questions: Why do animal cells have no chloroplasts - and how do animals eat instead?
segments.say: Two specialists: nucleus and chloroplast. The nucleus is the control centre holding the instructions; the chloroplast is the food factory trapping light. Only plants have the factory, which is why animals must eat food made by others.

questions: What single word describes the firm cell - and its opposite?
segments.say: Why plants stand up straight. Water fills the vacuole until it pushes the membrane hard against the wall: turgid and firm. Drain the water and the plant wilts. Mime it with your hands: full, firm; empty, limp.

questions: What sits between cell and organ on the ladder?
Give the leaf example from cell to system.
segments.say: Cells team up: the organisation ladder. Cell, tissue, organ, system - leaf cell, leaf tissue, leaf, shoot system. Before we finish, work through the trap section of your student notes in pairs, check the worksheet answers, then do the exit ticket on your own.
segments.watchFor: The cell membrane is a solid wall that blocks everything from entering or leaving. Listen for students who say nothing can enter a cell, or who call the membrane a wall. Send them back to scene 3: The membrane is selectively permeable: it lets some things through and keeps others out.
